payload.title: Vector Database Selection for 10 Million Documents

sections.heading: Findings
sections.body: Cohere provides 10 million 768-dimensional vectors [E1]. Pinecone: 45-80ms (serverless), 20-40ms (pod-based) [E2]; Pinecone demonstrates the lowest latency, with a p95 latency of 40-50 milliseconds [E6] Pinecone supports 5,000-10,000 QPS [E7]. Pinecone pricing starts at $0.096/hr per pod (~$70/month) and can reach $200-400/month for larger deployments [E8]. Weaviate: 30-70ms (with hybrid search adding 10-20ms) [E3]; In contrast, Weaviate shows a slightly higher latency range of 50-70 milliseconds [E9] Milvus query latency p95 is 25-50ms depending on index type and configuration [E4]; Zilliz Cloud (Milvus) costs $200-400 [E5]. If dataset does not fit in memory and speed is not critical, SQLite can be used as storage [E10]; otherwise Weaviate, Qdrant and Elasticsearch are good options [E11].

sections.heading: Details
sections.body: Pinecone demonstrates the lowest latency, with a p95 latency of 40-50 milliseconds [E6]; Pinecone supports 5,000-10,000 QPS [E7] Its cost starts around $70/month for 10M vectors and can rise to $200-400/month for larger usage [E8]. Weaviate provides hybrid search capabilities but exhibits higher latency (30-70ms base, plus 10-20ms for hybrid) [E3][E9]. Milvus/Zilliz Cloud delivers latency in the 25-50ms range with cost estimated $200-400 [E4][E5]. When memory constraints or speed are not priorities, SQLite can serve as a simple storage fallback [E10]; otherwise Weaviate, Qdrant, and Elasticsearch remain viable alternatives [E11].

citations.span: Pinecone demonstrates the lowest latency, with a p95 latency of 40-50 milliseconds, making it particularly well-suited for real-time applications where responsiveness is crucial.
Pinecone supports 5,000-10,000 QPS, making it efficient for moderate-scale applications.

Pricing for Pinecone in 2026 starts at $0.096/hr per pod, which equates to approximately $70/month for 10M vectors. For larger deployments, costs can range from $200–$400/month, depending on the number of pods and usage.
In contrast, Weaviate shows a slightly higher latency range of 50-70 milliseconds, which may still be acceptable for many applications but could introduce minor delays in highly interactive systems.
Milvus: 25-50ms (depends on index type and configuration)
Finally, if your dataset does not fit in memory, and you do not care much about the speed of nearest neighbor search, you can use SQLite as storage.
Otherwise, Weaviate, Qdrant and Elasticsearch are good options.
